name: Oti
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog refs are ethnographic/wordlist only (Borba 1908, Baldus 1954, Nimuendaju); no phonological description of Oti exists

new_statements.quote: Os Xavantes repellem a poligamia, e não empregam suas armas contra o homem. Quando quazi todas as palavras de vocabulario dos Caiuás e dos Coroados terminam por silabas agudas, as dos xavantes têm quazi todas o acento agudo na penultima. Resta-me aprezentar um rezumido vocabulario comparado d'essas trez linguas, com os termos correspondentes do guarani e do portuguez.
new_statements.translation: The Xavantes reject polygamy and do not use their weapons against man. Whereas almost all the words of the vocabulary of the Caiuás [Kaiowá Guarani] and of the Coroados [Kaingang] end in stressed (oxytone) syllables, those of the Xavantes [= Oti] almost all have the acute accent [stress] on the penultimate. It remains for me to present a brief comparative vocabulary of these three languages, with the corresponding Guarani and Portuguese terms.
new_statements.citation: Quadros, Francisco Raimundo Ewerton. 1892. Memoria sobre os trabalhos de exploração e observação efetuada pela secção da comissão militar encarregada da linha telegráfica de Uberaba a Cuiabá, de fevereiro a junho de 1889. Revista do Instituto Histórico e Geográfico Brasileiro 55(1):233-260.
new_statements.locator: p. 255 (end of the section on the 'Xavantes' of São Paulo, immediately before the Vocabulario Comparado, pp. 256-259); quoted verbatim in Baldus 1954: 82
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE: Opened (page image of PDF p. 25 = printed p. 255 of; the PDF itself has no text layer beyond the etnolinguistica cover sheet). The passage is there word for word: 'Os Xavantes repellem a poligamia, e não empregam suas armas contra o homem. / Quando quazi todas as palavras de vocabulario dos Caiuás e dos Coroados terminam por silabas agudas, as dos xavantes têm quazi todas o acento agudo na penultima. / Resta-me aprezentar um rezumido vocabulario comparado d'essas trez linguas, com os termos correspondentes do guarani e do portuguez.' The only difference from the report's quote is that the original sets these as three separate paragraphs; wording, spelling (quazi, aprezentar, rezumido…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent in Oti falls on the penultimate syllable in almost all words, in contrast to the final stress of neighbouring Guarani (Kaiowá) and Kaingang; an impressionistic observation by the collector of a ~50-item wordlist (1889), whose transcriptions mark the accent accordingly (Inuáde, Atáve, Guiáde, Tuásia, Catiága, Folháhe, Concéde).
new_statements.exceptions: Only the hedge 'quazi todas' (almost all); Quadros's own list has at least one final-accented form (Achô 'fire'). Not mentioned by Quadros but relevant: Nimuendajú's independent Oti list (in Ihering 1912: 255-260) writes the accent on the final syllable in many items (koaká, daká, kakí, iská, fugidó, kōsidé, gna'atá, otí), so the penult generalisation is not secure.
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation forms elicited from a wordlist; no word/phrase distinction possible. The language is extinct and attested only by ~110 words, so no fuller description can ever exist.
new_statements.identity_note: Quadros (1892) calls the group 'Xavantes' (of the São Paulo sertão, = Curuton of the Coroados, Oto of the Guarani); this is the Oti of Campos Novos / Paranapanema (otii1244), not the Akwẽ-Xavante of Mato Grosso (xava1240) nor the Ofayé-'Chavante' (ofay1240). Ihering (1895, 1904) and Baldus (1954: 82) explicitly identify Quadros's 'Xavante' vocabulary as Oti. The language is extinct; the entire corpus is ~110 words in three wordlists (Quadros 1892, Borba 1908, Nimuendajú in Ihering 1912).

sources.locator: p. 255 (end of the section on the 'Xavantes' of São Paulo, immediately before the Vocabulario Comparado, pp. 256-259); quoted verbatim in Baldus 1954: 82
sources.note: p. 255: whereas almost all Caiuá and Coroado words end in stressed (aguda) syllables, the Xavante [=Oti] words 'têm quazi todas o acento agudo na penultima'; the vocabulary pp. 256-259 writes accent marks on the Xavante forms (Inuáde, Donduède, Atáve, Guiáde, Tuásia, Catiága, Jatâme, Folháhe, Concéde; but also Achô).

sources.citation: Baldus, Herbert. 1954. Os Oti. Revista do Museu Paulista n.s. 8:79-92.
sources.note: p. 82 quotes Quadros (1892:254-255) verbatim, including the sentence that Xavante [Oti] words almost all have the accent on the penultimate; Baldus adds nothing of his own on accent and identifies Quadros's 'Xavantes' as the Oti.

sources.citation: Nikulin, Andrey. 2020. Proto-Macro-Jê: um estudo reconstrutivo. Tese de doutorado, Universidade de Brasília. Sec. 2.7 'Otí e Macro-Jê', pp. 78-80.
sources.note: Nothing; lists the three Oti sources (Quadros 1892, Borba 1908:73-76, Nimuendajú in Ihering 1912) and compares basic vocabulary with Proto-Macro-Jê/Chiquitano/Tupí, concluding Oti cannot be related to them.

sources.citation: Ihering, Hermann von. 1912. A ethnographia do Brazil meridional. Actas del XVII Congreso Internacional de Americanistas (Buenos Aires 1910), 250-263 [contains 'Vocabulario dos Chavantes de Campos Novos' collected by Curt Nimuendajú (Unckel), pp. 255-260].
sources.note: No prose statement on accent. Nimuendajú's forms carry accent marks, many of them on the FINAL syllable (koaká, daká, kakí, ko'ajé, iská, fugidó, kōsidé, gna'atá, otí, iskentál) alongside penult/other (apíla, béia, tuáta, káibe, naôdj) -- data that sit uneasily with Quadros's penult generalisation.

sources.citation: Borba, Telemaco. 1908. Actualidade Indigena (Paraná, Brazil). Curitiba: Impressora Paranaense. [Vocabulario Caiguá-Chavante, pp. 72-76]
sources.note: Intro (p. 72) and footnotes (p. 73) only describe letters: Chavante has l, strong (guttural) r, a z like English th, j as in Spanish; nothing on accent; forms mostly written without accent marks (Diélsede, Uirgêlem, Bóje are exceptions).
